verdict: Airbnb grew revenue 18% to $2.7B as guests booked $29.2B of stays, but net income was just $160M — a one-time $70M tax-asset adjustment tied to new U.S. minimum-tax rules ate much of the quarter's profit.

segments.name: Stays & experiences
segments.note: Service fees on every stay, experience and service booked. Airbnb reports a single revenue stream; the bookings behind it were worth $29.2B in gross booking value.

opex.name: Operations and support
opex.note: Supporting hosts and guests — customer service, trust & safety and host insurance.

opex.name: Product development
opex.note: Building the app and new products like experiences and services.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Marketing to win travelers and hosts.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day.

takeaways.title: Guests spent freely
takeaways.text: Gross booking value rose 19% to $29.2B and nights and seats booked rose 9% to 156.2M — demand and pricing both helped, with a currency tailwind on top.

takeaways.title: A seasonal cash gusher
takeaways.text: Free cash flow was $1.7B — 64% of revenue — because guests pay when they book, months before many stays happen. Q1 is always Airbnb's biggest cash quarter.

takeaways.title: A tax quirk cut profit
takeaways.text: Net income was $160M on $281M of pre-tax profit — a 43% tax rate — because of a one-time $70M deferred-tax adjustment from new U.S. minimum-tax rules.

oneTimers: The tax bill includes a one-time adjustment of approximately $70M to certain deferred tax assets as a result of changes to the U.S. Corporate Alternative Minimum Tax effective in Q1 2026; Airbnb expects its full-year effective tax rate to be in the high teens.
otherDetail: Interest and other items netted +$195M: $155M of interest earned (Airbnb holds billions in guest payments before stays happen), plus $40M of other income.
